title: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman LLC Urges Bloom Energy Corporation Investors to Act: Class Action Filed Alleging Investor Harm
author: Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman Llc
description: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Bloom Energy Corporation alleging that the company made false and misleading statements regarding its reliance on scandium sourced from China through intermediaries. The lawsuit covers investors who purchased Bloom Energy securities between February 27, 2026 and July 8, 2026. Investors have until September 28, 2026 to request appointment as lead plaintiff.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company is accused of making false and misleading statements about its business operations, specifically regarding undisclosed reliance on scandium sourced from China through intermediaries. This represents alleged securities fraud and investor harm.

title: BE INVESTOR DEADLINE APPROACHING: Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP Reminds Bloom Energy (BE) Investors of Securities Class Action Lawsuit Deadline on September 28, 2026
author: Faruqi & Faruqi, Llp
description: Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP is investigating securities fraud claims against Bloom Energy Corporation, alleging the company made false statements about its supply chain by understating reliance on Chinese scandium sourced through intermediaries. Following a July 8, 2026 report by Hunterbrook Media exposing the company's China-linked supply routes, Bloom Energy's stock fell 5.7%. Investors who purchased securities between February 27, 2025 and July 8, 2026 have until September 28, 2026 to seek lead plaintiff status in the class action lawsuit.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company faces securities fraud allegations for making false or misleading statements about its supply chain and understating reliance on Chinese scandium. The exposure of these practices resulted in a 5.7% stock price decline, and investors are being encouraged to join a class action lawsuit with a September 28, 2026 deadline.

title: Bloom Energy's Backlog Is 5 Times This Year's Expected Revenue. Here's How Fast It Can Actually Build.
author: Daniel Sparks
description: Bloom Energy disclosed a $20 billion backlog in February, with $6 billion in product orders and $14 billion in long-term service contracts. While the company plans to double its Fremont factory capacity to 2 gigawatts by end of 2026 and has raised revenue guidance twice this year, the analyst cautions that the stock's valuation at 56x forward P/E assumes full-speed conversion for years, which may be overly optimistic.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the company shows strong operational momentum with 130-166% YoY revenue growth, doubled guidance raises, and a substantial $20B backlog, the analyst expresses caution about the stock's valuation at 56x forward P/E, suggesting the market may be pricing in overly optimistic conversion assumptions. The backlog is real but conversion timelines are uncertain.

title: Better Energy Sector ETF: Vanguard's VDE Focused on Oil and Gas vs. the iShares ICLN Targeting Clean Energy
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: The Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE) and iShares Global Clean Energy ETF (ICLN) represent opposite ends of the energy spectrum. VDE focuses on traditional U.S. oil and gas giants with a 46.8% one-year return, lower expense ratio (0.09%), higher dividend yield (2.3%), and greater stability. ICLN targets international renewable energy with higher growth potential but experienced a 57.2% maximum drawdown and declining performance in 2026 due to unfavorable Trump Administration policies toward renewables.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong one-year return of 46.8%, lowest expense ratio at 0.09%, highest dividend yield at 2.3%, larger AUM ($13.2B) providing better liquidity, and lower volatility (beta 0.50) make it attractive for income and stability-focused investors.

Offers high growth potential in renewable energy sector with exposure to AI-driven green energy demand, but faces headwinds from Trump Administration policies, declining 2026 performance, higher volatility (beta 1.10), deeper maximum drawdown (57.2%), and higher expense ratio (0.38%).

title: FLNC or BE: Which Alternative Energy Stock Is Worth Buying Now?
author: Na
description: In a comparison of two alternate energy stocks, Bloom Energy (BE) emerges as the more attractive investment despite Fluence Energy's (FLNC) lower valuation. BE benefits from stronger price performance, consistent earnings beats, and growing demand from AI data centers, while FLNC faces manufacturing delays, guidance cuts, and battery oversupply concerns.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong year-to-date price performance, consistent earnings beats (164.1% average), doubled revenues to $1.8B in H1 2026, raised 2026 guidance to $3.9-$4.2B, expanded $25B partnership with Brookfield for AI power infrastructure, and positioned to benefit from rising demand for reliable on-site power and AI data center expansion. Rated Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Reported wider-than-expected Q3 loss and revenue miss, cut fiscal 2026 guidance significantly (revenues down from $3B to $2.4B, EBITDA loss widened from -$10M to -$200M), facing manufacturing delays and supply-chain challenges, weak earnings surprise history (114.5% average miss), and concerns about battery oversupply. Rated Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell). However, strong international demand and restructuring efforts provide some mitigation.
